extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners (Korean jurisdiction / KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: KIPO examination guidelines on Article 30 (disclosure exceptions / grace period) and the beginning of Article 29 (inventive step), describing eligibility, procedural requirements, evidentiary standards, and substantive criteria for inventive step determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 30 disclosure-exception eligibility (disclosed by right-holder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention is disclosed by a person with the right to obtain a patent before filing, the invention is not considered disclosed if: (a) the invention is disclosed by a person with the right to obtain a patent; (b) the invention is filed by a person with the right to obtain a patent within twelve months (six months if filing date earlier than March 14, 2012) of the date on which the invention is disclosed; (c) the intent of being applied by Article 30 is stated in the application; and (d) documents proving the relevant facts are submitted within thirty days of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the date of disclosure is unspecified, the first day of the month and year of disclosure may be applied. The 'intention' may be indicated by checking the box for disclosure exception on the application cover sheet; evidential documents may be submitted simultaneously with filing or within 30 days (with later special timings for some filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 30 disclosure-exception eligibility (disclosed against intention)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is disclosed against the intention of a person with the right to obtain a patent, the applicant must file within twelve months (six months in certain earlier cases) of the date on which the invention is disclosed; there is no need to state the purport (intention) in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an invention was disclosed against the intention of the right-holder is determined by considering the right-holder's clear intention at the time of disclosure. Proof of the disclosure-against-intent may be judged case-by-case and may be proved in various ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement and supporting documents timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to take advantage of Article 30 must submit a written statement of that intention to the Commissioner of KIPO when filing, and must submit documents proving the relevant facts within thirty days of the filing date of the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding paragraph 2, where supplementary fee is paid, the proving document may instead be submitted within specified amendment periods (e.g., within the amendment period in Article 47(1) or within 3 months from receipt of certified copy of grant or trial decision). For international applications, intention and evidence follow the reference date rules (Article 201(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate/extended submission periods (post-July 29, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on and after July 29, 2015, proving documents can be submitted within 3 months (provided it is before registration of a patent) from the date of receiving a certified copy of grant of patent or within the specified period to amend a specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same regulation applies to utility model registration applications. Examiner shall issue a notice of all grounds for rejection at once if applicant did not state exception at filing but may later invoke grace period within these alternative windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination for disclosure exception claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon an application indicating the purport of claiming disclosure exception, the examiner conducts formalities examination on whether the application is submitted within the statutory period (12 or 6 months) and whether the disclosure was made by a person with the right to obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office issues a notice to correct deficiencies when: (i) discloser differs from filer/inventor; (ii) application filed after statutory period; (iii) wrong disclosure date or type or incorrect supporting information; (iv) submitted documents insufficient to prove relevant facts. Failure to amend within designated period invalidates the Article 30 claiming proceeding (the filing remains effective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters required for examining sufficiency of evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters required for examination on disclosure exception are: (i) disclosure date, (ii) discloser, (iii) disclosure type, and (iv) content of the disclosed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency is judged based on whether these matters can be confirmed from the evidential documents. For exhibition disclosures, supplementary documents such as copies of program, catalog, pamphlets, and photos of exhibits may be requested. Where fact relations are questioned, additional documents proving hosting party, venue, exhibitor, etc., can be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination when disclosure-exception claim is presented
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner reviews all submitted documents and examines the invention if no defects are found. Disclosures that fall under Article 30 are recognized as non-prior art in the examination where Article 29(1) or (2) applies to the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the proceeding claiming non-disclosure fails because of deficiencies in application or documents, the submitted documents may be used as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple disclosures / inseparable disclosures handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a right-holder discloses an invention several times before filing, in principle the Article 30 proceeding shall be taken for each disclosure; however, the indication of intention need not specify each disclosure if the intention to apply the exception is recognized and evidential documents for the disclosure are submitted within 30 days from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a disclosure is 'inseparably related' to one or more disclosures (examples: multi-day tests, test+distributed explanation, first/second edition of a publication, collections and oral presentation, oral presentation+lecture booklet, lecture tour, exhibition display+catalog), subsequent disclosures may be exempted from submitting proof. Twelve-month period is calculated from the earliest disclosure date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party intervening disclosure (between initial disclosure and filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third person publicly discloses the same invention between the initial disclosure (claimed under Article 30) and the filing date, the examiner shall reject the application of the original filer for lack of novelty, except in the obvious case that the third-person disclosure was made by learning from the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will notify grounds for rejection and the applicant must establish that the third-party disclosure occurred after learning from the (non-considered) disclosure, or that the invention was filed against the applicant's intention. Otherwise, the application may be rejected for lacking novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous filings and Article 36 consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant A files within the grace period and claims Article 30, and on the same filing date a third person files application B for the same invention, Article 36(2) applies: A and B are related and the applicants should reach agreement on who will obtain the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because B is filed after the invention was disclosed, B is deemed to lack novelty and its applicant may not obtain a patent. Examiner instructs applicants to consult and report results under Article 36(6) rather than issuing a rejection for novelty immediately. If B withdraws, A may obtain the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open / publication bars Article 30 application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application was laid open or registered in Korea or a foreign country under treaties/laws, Article 30 cannot be applied to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laying-open done under normal filing proceedings is not voluntary by applicant and thus Article 30 does not apply; however, if the Office mistakenly lays open an application before it should be, that disclosure may be regarded as against the applicant's intention and Article 30 may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims and Article 30 advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files claiming priority, to take advantage of Article 30 the applicant shall file in Korea within twelve months (six months in earlier cases) of the date to which Article 30 applies. However, if the earlier application was filed in KIPO within the statutory period of disclosure, the applicant may take advantage even if the subsequent application is not filed within the twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows certain priority chains to preserve the disclosure-exception benefit if the earlier domestic application was timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of disclosures covered by the grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures to which the grace period applies include: disclosure by a person with entitlement to obtain a patent; disclosure by a third party asked to disclose by the right-holder; and disclosure by a third party referencing the invention with permission (including implied permission) from the right-holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: entrusted disclosure where inventor/right-holder's name is stated; press releases or scripts sent to newspapers; news or papers by third parties that mention the inventor/company and cite the invention; company printed catalogs. If a third-party disclosure was at the request of the right-holder, facts that the discloser acted at the right-holder's request should be proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors / presenters evidentiary rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more persons jointly make an invention or file an application, and among presenters who disclosed the invention at least one presenter is the inventor or applicant, Article 30 may apply without separate proof that the inventor/applicant disclosed the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no relation between the inventor/applicant and the person who disclosed the invention, the applicant must submit: (i) a document proving the presenter is the person with the right to obtain a patent; (ii) a document proving the invention was disclosed at the request of the entitled person; and (iii) a document proving the presenter obtained permission for referencing the invention from the entitled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications — declaration and evidence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For international (PCT) applications deemed filed to KIPO, a person can declare exceptions to lack of novelty in PCT Request Box No. VIII(v); that declaration is deemed to meet application cover-sheet requirements if a document proving the relevant facts is legitimately submitted within 30 days from the reference date under Article 200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where such declaration and supporting evidence are submitted within the specified period, the international application shall be examined as if it included a regular domestic claiming of exceptions to lack of novelty (refer to PCT Rule 4.17). For national phase entries, similar timing applies relative to the national entry reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner issuance of all grounds for rejection when exception not declared at filing (post-2015 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on and after July 29, 2015, even if the applicant did not state at filing that the invention was disclosed, because the applicant can invoke grace period within 3 months after grant or during designated amendment periods, the examiner shall issue a notice of all grounds for rejection at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant remedies grounds for rejection by later claiming the disclosure exception but the examiner finds other grounds based on other prior documents, the examiner shall issue a first office action to notify those new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 29 inventive-step requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention that can be made easily by a person with ordinary skill in the art from an invention referred to in Article 29(1) prior to filing is not patentable (i.e., lacks inventive step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purport is to refuse patents for inventions that could have been easily made by a person skilled in the art because granting such patents would hamper technological progress. 'Inventive step' itself is not defined in the Act; the practical test is whether the claimed invention could have been easily made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'prior to filing' for novelty/inventive-step purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Prior to filing of a patent application' means the definite time, in hours and minutes, of the filing of an application (Korean local time). If a public disclosure's time precedes the filing time in Korean local time, it is considered prior art under Article 29(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact filing time (hours/minutes) rather than merely the filing date when determining whether a disclosure is prior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'person skilled in the art'
rubrics_metrics.description: A hypothetical person who has common general knowledge in the art, the ability to use ordinary technical means (experimentation, analysis, manufacture), the ability to exercise ordinary creativity in selecting materials and changing designs, and who can comprehend, based on their own knowledge, all technical matters regarding the state of the art at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An expert in the technical field is one able to comprehend all technical matters relevant to the problem to be solved by the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'state of the art' for inventive-step analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'state of the art' at filing includes the inventions referred to in Article 29(1), common general knowledge, and other publicly known technical matters; it also relates to all information relevant to the technical field described in the claims, including ordinary methods to conduct daily work and experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both explicit prior-art disclosures and routine/common techniques when assessing whether a claimed invention would have been obvious to the person skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Could have been easily made' — practical test for inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an invention 'could have been easily made by a person skilled in the art' refers to whether such a person could have easily conceived the claimed invention by exercising ordinary creativity or based on motivation induced from prior art disclosures before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This centers on whether ordinary creativity and routine motivation would have led from the prior art to the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for determining inventive step (claim-by-claim, combination of references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the invention described in each claim could have been easily made by a person skilled in the art based on prior-art reference(s) prior to filing; if yes, that claim lacks inventive step. Determination is to be made for each claim separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there are multiple claims, make the inventive-step determination claim-by-claim. Notifying applicants of lack of novelty is different from notifying lack of inventive step, but an examiner may notify both together if novelty is lacking.
